name: Triveni Engineering & Industries Ltd
title: Triveni Engineering & Industries Ltd - 532356 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Sugar and distillery turned around on lower grain cost and record distillery volumes, but PTB Q4 order finalisation slipped and cane crush fell 8.8% to 8.25 mt; FY26 PAT ₹268.7 cr up 12.8%.

summary.headline: Triveni FY26 revenue rose 10.6% to ₹6,291 crore and PBT reached ₹378 crore, while Q4 revenue dipped on PTB order slippage.
summary.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue net of excise was ₹6,291 crore (up 10.6%), with the net profit at ₹268.7 crore (up 12.8%) and EBITDA of about ₹624 crore (16.9% margin). Q4 revenue was just over ₹1,500 crore, slightly down YoY, due to scaled-down ethanol dispatches to OMCs and short delivery deferment in Power Transmission. The distillery segment staged a sharp turnaround on record volumes and lower maize costs, while sugar crush fell 8.8% to 8.25 million tonnes. The composite scheme became effective on 19 May 2026, with the TPTL demerger and listing targeted by end-August 2026.

segments.name: Sugar
segments.commentary: Revenue grew almost 13% and PBIT was about ₹272 crore (marginal growth). Crush fell 8.8% to 8.25 million tonnes, with West UP down 17%; gross recovery rose 26 bps to 11.06%, and net sugar output was about 913,000 tonnes. Domestic sales volume was 9.79 lakh tonnes at ₹40,680/tonne.

segments.name: Distillery
segments.commentary: Record production and sales volumes with FY26 revenue net of excise of ₹1,550 crore. Realisation averaged ₹61/litre (lower due to FCI rice mix), and grain made up 56% of ethanol sales (maize about 33%). Management said conversion and raw-material costs fell significantly.

segments.name: Power Transmission (PTB/gearboxes)
segments.commentary: Q4 was weak on steam-turbine order finalisation delays and West Asia-related deferrals, with finished gearboxes awaiting export. Order book closed at just under ₹500 crore (up 25% YoY). Aftermarket was about 40% of gears sales in FY26 versus over 30% historically; PBIT margin is about 35%.

segments.name: Water
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 15% to over ₹270 crore on EPC execution. Closing order book was just over ₹1,500 crore, of which about ₹1,077 crore is long-duration O&M. FY26 order inflow was ₹165 crore, and receivables are about ₹125–150 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the gearbox CapEx of ₹340 crore (approved in three tranches) to finish by September 2026. About ₹231 crore was spent by 31 March 2026, with ~₹109 crore to be spent in Q1 and Q2 FY27; this is expected to support about ₹700 crore of gearbox output.
Management expects exports to exceed 50% of PTB original-equipment sales in the very near future.

National sugar production is estimated at 27.8 million tonnes; Triveni's closing sugar stock is projected at 4.6–4.8 million tonnes. The sugar season is expected to start in the second half of October 2026.
Ethanol: 17.18 crore litres allocated under cycle one; further OMC and private tender allocations are expected shortly. Management also said the ethanol tender this year was a disappointment.
Short-term borrowings are expected to fall sharply from April and reach almost zero by September or October 2026.
TPTL demerger: record date for Triveni shareholders expected to be set within about four weeks, with listing targeted by end-August 2026.
capex_capacity: Gearbox CapEx of ₹340 crore approved in three tranches; ₹231 crore incurred by 31 March 2026, of which ₹78 crore was for the defence facility, with completion targeted by September 2026.
New multi-modal test facility in Mysore is now fully operable; defence facility machinery commissioned in Q4 and test facility to be installed over the next couple of quarters.
Shamli distillery, which has not operated since acquisition, is expected to add capacity without new CapEx; some distillery capacities are being debottlenecked.
Sugar CapEx currently under way is aimed only at lowering production costs; varietal replacement is ongoing.
Khatauli unit was the only one in West UP to cross 200 lakh quintals crushing capacity this season.
demand_pricing: Ex-mill refined sugar prices were about ₹42.20/kg, and sulphitation sugar about ₹41.50/kg; refined sugar averaged ₹41.32/kg in FY26. Inventory of ~60 lakh quintals was valued at ₹38.1/kg.
Cane price rose ₹300/tonne in UP; management said recoveries and cost measures absorbed it.
Maize cost is about ₹0.75–0.80/kg lower than last year, per the distillery head, though rupee depreciation raises export exposure.
PTB enquiry book is strong and skewed to exports; management said Q1 FY27 saw a surge of domestic enquiries after capex slowdown in Q3–Q4.
Water segment demand is supported by stricter ZLD and liquid discharge rules; management expects more orders soon.
Defence orders are in the double-digit to triple-digit crore range with 1–4 year delivery; RENK is increasing tender presence but management said it is not winning more high-speed orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of PTB sales between original-equipment and aftermarket, and how is the distribution network built?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not split OE and replacement revenue; aftermarket was about 40% of gears sales in FY26, versus above 30% historically. It is building agency partners abroad and treats AVL approvals as a multi-year process.

qa_highlights.question: Are the aftermarket and gas-segment opportunities growing, and is RENK a competitive threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gas qualification work is underway for data-centre-linked gas turbines and engines and is expected to yield AVL wins within a few quarters. RENK is more visible in tenders but management does not think it is winning more high-speed orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA/PBIT outlook for PTB after the demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Suresh Taneja said PTB has consistently maintained about 35% PBIT and expects the same trend to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ethanol feedstock mix and FY27 grain-based EBITDA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Maize was about 33% of ethanol mix (down from 44%) because the ESY tender required 40% of grain allocation to come from FCI rice; grain was 56% of total. Management said FY27 depends on the next tender and government policy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital and water receivables picture?
qa_highlights.answer: Total receivables are about ₹500 crore, including ₹125–150 crore from water. Higher short-term borrowings reflect higher cane price working capital, which should fall from April.

qa_highlights.question: What is the defence business order size and the CapEx split?
qa_highlights.answer: Defence orders are double-digit to triple-digit crore; about 40% of the pending ₹109 crore CapEx goes to defence.

risks_watch: Q4 PTB slippage: export-bound gearboxes sitting in finished goods and steam-turbine order finalisation delays linked to West Asia.
Sugar: El Niño and a possible Super El Niño could affect monsoon and crop yields; cane diversion to gur and khandsari hit crush this season.
Ethanol: delays in OMC and private tender allocations, a legal dispute in South India, and government preference for FCI rice over maize could compress distillery margins.
TPTL demerger and listing timing (end-August 2026), plus approvals needed for record date and share dispersal.
Q1 FY27 board results for TEIL and TPTL, and whether PTB's order conversion picks up.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term outlook for sugar, distillery and PTB exports, but cautious and defensive on Q4 PTB performance and on some numerical questions, which management declined to answer. Management repeatedly declined to give forward-looking numbers on gearbox demand, crushing and conversion costs.
key_quotes: It is a significant blip, but it is a blip of one quarter in time due to global changes where we had a lot of gearboxes that were scheduled to be exported that are in finished goods in the business and are not exported and will be exported during this quarter and some in the following quarter.
In FY26, the aftermarket share was about 40% of overall gears.
We don't typically give out data to segment between original equipment sales as well as replacement sales of original equipment.
I'm delighted to inform you that the composite scheme of arrangement is effective from the 19th of May, 2026 after the approval of the NCLT.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated revenue from operations (net of excise), FY26
Exceptional charge, FY26 (new labour codes retroactive impact)

adds.what: Gearbox capacity expansion, ~₹700 crore output from ₹340 crore capex (₹231 cr spent by 31 Mar 2026, ~₹109 cr to go in Q1-Q2 FY27)
Defence test facility in Mysore (multi-modal), fully operable; defence machinery commissioned in Q4, test facility installation over next couple of quarters
Shamli distillery (not operated since acquisition) expected to add capacity without new capex; some distillery debottlenecking

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; PTB PBIT margin held at ~35% and gearbox capex of ₹340 cr (₹700 cr output) to complete by Sept 2026, backed by a gear order book just under ₹500 cr (+25% YoY) and Water order book ~₹1,500 cr, though Q4 revenue dipped slightly YoY and ethanol tender allocations disappointed.
